gaps.sentence: Nobody explained the reason ___ the flight was cancelled.
gaps.explanation: 'Why' introduces the cause after 'the reason'; it means 'for which'.

gaps.sentence: July and August are the months ___ most Italians take their holidays.
gaps.explanation: 'When' means 'in which' after time expressions; the clause describes when the action happens.

gaps.sentence: It was the best meal ___ I have ever eaten.
gaps.hint: after a superlative, this pronoun is preferred
gaps.explanation: After superlatives ('the best ...'), 'that' is the preferred relative pronoun in defining clauses.

gaps.sentence: There was something ___ smelled awful in the kitchen.
gaps.explanation: After 'something', 'that' is the standard relative pronoun; 'what' cannot follow 'something'.

gaps.sentence: We must decide ___ to do next.
gaps.explanation: 'What to do' is the standard pattern meaning 'the thing that we should do'.

gaps.sentence: That was the year ___ the company nearly went bankrupt.
gaps.hint: time: it happened in that year
gaps.explanation: 'When' is used after 'the year'; 'which' would need 'in which'.

gaps.sentence: The lawyers, against ___ the case was brought, denied everything.
gaps.hint: the case was brought against them
gaps.explanation: 'Against whom' is the formal relative pattern; 'who' and 'that' cannot follow prepositions.

gaps.sentence: The discussion got to a stage ___ nobody was listening any more.
gaps.explanation: 'A stage where ...' means 'a stage at which ...'; the clause has its own subject and verb, so 'which' is impossible.
